summary.text: An embedded normalizing flow is combined with an empirical-likelihood estimator under moment restrictions to facilitate simulation-based parameter estimation for physical system models. This framework transforms unknown complex residual distributions into simple base distributions, enabling gradient-based updates of the simulation parameters. The approach provides an information-theoretic interpretation and serves as a surrogate model for quantifying model discrepancies and conducting sensitivity analysis.

target_user.text: No evidence in the bundle; hypothesis to test: Open source users and package maintainers of statistical modeling tools such as lightgbmlss, xgboostlss, torchcfm, and lf2i.

jtbd.text: No evidence in the bundle; hypothesis to test: Perform simulation-based parameter estimation for computational simulation models of physical systems while handling unknown complex residual distributions.

value_prop.text: No evidence in the bundle; hypothesis to test: Enables end-to-end simulation-based parameter estimation by transforming complex residual distributions via embedded normalizing flows and imposing indirect constraints using empirical-likelihood estimators under moment restrictions.

riskiest_assumption.text: Axis V (viability) was designated as the riskiest assumption due to missing evidence in the bundle. The assumption is that users will adopt and pay for a simulation-based parameter estimation framework combining embedded normalizing flows and empirical-likelihood estimators.

mvp.text: Conduct customer interviews and a price acceptance test with potential users of simulation-based parameter estimation tools to test willingness to pay and viability of the embedded normalizing flow framework.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of 40 percent positive willingness to pay during price acceptance testing and validate demand in at least 5 out of 10 customer interviews.

kill_criteria.text: Fewer than 20 percent of interviewed prospective users express interest in adopting the simulation-based parameter estimation framework during customer interviews.
Zero prospective users accept the proposed pricing during price acceptance tests.
